input.quote: Garman agrees to indemnify Sparkling and hold it harmless from any and all losses, damages and expenses including without limitation, court costs, arbitration fees, penalties, fines, amounts paid in settlement of claims and reasonable legal fees and expenses of investigation (collectively the "Losses") which Sparkling or any of its respective officers or directors may incur due to a breach of this warranty.
input.rationale: Section 13 contains only an ownership statement; the operative indemnity sits in the following paragraph and is limited to Losses arising from breach of Garman's title/quiet-enjoyment warranty, with procure/replace/modify remedies at (a)-(c) and a ten-day notice condition. It is uncapped (Section 15 disapplies the liability limit to Section 13), which is better than the fallback 3x super-cap, and it carries no Customer-modification/combination/specification exclusions. However it fails the fallback because there is no refund where the procure/modify/replace remedies are unavailable, and it fails the preferred position on materially more: no express duty to defend, no coverage of Sparkling's affiliates, no indemnity for Garman's breach of applicable law, Garman-caused unauthorised access to our data, or Garman's gross negligence/wilful misconduct, and no allocation of defence control or cooperation. We therefore target the preferred position with a single added paragraph rather than importing the fallback super-cap, which would weaken our current uncapped position. No Sparkling indemnity exists anywhere (Sections 3 and 20 included), so the added sentence simply confirms that any such obligation stays limited to our content and our breach of law.

mappings.element: Vendor has an express duty to defend Customer and its affiliates.
Vendor indemnifies Customer and its affiliates against third-party claims.
Vendor indemnity covers claims that Services or Deliverables infringe intellectual property rights.
Vendor indemnity covers Vendor's breach of applicable law.
Vendor indemnity covers a data breach caused by Vendor.
Vendor indemnity covers Vendor's gross negligence and wilful misconduct.
The indemnification procedure requires notice of a claim.
The indemnification procedure allocates control of the defence.
The indemnification procedure requires reasonable cooperation.
Customer indemnity is limited to Customer-provided content and Customer's breach of law.

proposal.summary: Add a Garman defence and indemnity covering IP infringement, breach of law, Garman-caused data breach and misconduct, with claim procedure and a cap on any Sparkling indemnity.
proposal.comment: [Playbook] Section 13 gives us only a warranty-breach indemnity with no duty to defend and nothing for Garman's breach of law, data breaches or misconduct, so we added our preferred Vendor indemnity with the standard notice/control/cooperation procedure and confirmed any Sparkling indemnity stays limited to our own content and legal breaches.

ops.text: In addition, Garman shall defend, indemnify and hold harmless Sparkling and its affiliates from and against any third-party claim, and all resulting Losses, to the extent arising out of (i) an allegation that the Work or the Maintenance Services infringe or misappropriate any intellectual property right; (ii) Garman's breach of applicable law; (iii) any unauthorized access to or disclosure of Sparkling's data or Confidential Information caused by Garman; or (iv) Garman's gross negligence or wilful misconduct. Sparkling shall notify Garman of any such claim, Garman shall control the defence and settlement of the claim, and Sparkling shall provide reasonable cooperation in the defence. Sparkling's indemnity obligations, if any, under this Agreement are limited to third-party claims arising out of content provided by Sparkling and Sparkling's breach of applicable law.
